title: Monocausal attribution bias in low-information populations
description: Research in political psychology (e.g., Tetlock's expert political judgment work) shows that low-information actors default to "hedgehog" thinking — single-cause explanatory models — while high-information actors ("foxes") maintain multi-causal frameworks. Anti-Zionism maps onto the hedgehog archetype: one root cause explains a wide range of Middle Eastern and global outcomes.
source: Tetlock, P. (2005). Expert Political Judgment; related survey data on foreign policy knowledge and Israel-Palestine opinion correlates

title: Campus anti-Zionism correlates with low foreign-policy literacy
description: Survey and polling data (e.g., Pew, Gallup, campus-specific surveys) suggest that intensity of anti-Zionist conviction among Western activist populations inversely correlates with ability to identify basic geopolitical facts (e.g., naming parties to regional conflicts, identifying map locations, distinguishing Sunni/Shia dynamics). This is consistent with the thesis that anti-Zionism attracts the strategically unexposed rather than creating unsophistication.
source: Pew Research Center polling on Middle East knowledge; Gallup foreign affairs literacy surveys; various campus survey instruments 2015-2024

title: Analogous monocausal frameworks in other domains
description: The pattern of unsophisticated populations adopting single-villain explanatory models is not unique to anti-Zionism. Anti-globalization movements blame "the WTO," right-wing populisms blame immigrants, conspiracy movements blame shadowy elites. In each case, the monocausal framework is adopted by those who lack domain expertise, suggesting the causal direction runs from ignorance to framework adoption, not vice versa.
source: Comparative analysis of populist movements; Mudde (2004) on populist ideology; Hofstadter (1964) on paranoid style in politics

title: Sophisticated anti-Zionist actors exist as counterexamples
description: Some geopolitically sophisticated actors — certain international relations scholars, diplomats, regional specialists — hold anti-Zionist positions derived from detailed analysis rather than ignorance. This partially undermines the universality of the thesis, though the thesis claims to describe population-level tendencies rather than individual cases.
source: Academic literature in critical IR theory; statements by experienced diplomats and area specialists
